pairs.a: The Quillon Press warehouse ships about 1,200 parcels per day on average.
pairs.b: The Quillon Press warehouse typically sends out around 400 parcels a day.
pairs.rationale: "On average" and "typically" name the same central value in other words; the old rule read a statistic word on one side only as two different statistics.

pairs.a: The Quillon Press warehouse ships about 1,200 parcels per day on average.
pairs.b: No more than 800 parcels are ever dispatched from the Quillon Press warehouse in a single day.
pairs.rationale: A cap and an average of the same quantity are comparable (an average cannot exceed the maximum). A bound is not a statistic.

pairs.a: Fernhill Rowing Club allows a maximum of 40 rowers on its competitive squad.
pairs.b: Fernhill Rowing Club caps its competitive squad at 30 members.
pairs.rationale: "Caps … at 30" is a maximum. Two different maxima for the same thing are a limit near-miss, not an observation inside a limit.

pairs.a: The team at Fenwick Hospice meets every Wednesday.
pairs.b: The team moved its weekly meeting to Thursdays.
pairs.rationale: "Weekly" is a schedule word on one side only, not a statistic.
